Subject: Quick sanity check: units/$ assumptions for pilot

Hi Rohan / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — HelioHealth is excited to move toward a small pilot. Before we lock dates, procurement needs a clear sanity check on the units-per-dollar assumptions so finance can sign off. High-level ask below: can Redwood confirm whether our expected monthly spend range and MAP gating numbers look plausible?

Helio baseline:
- Avg concurrent requests: ~150–250 req/s (peak bursts to 400 for 30–60s)
- Typical prompt length (tokens in): 120 tokens; expected response avg: 180 tokens
- User journeys: ~60% short Q&A, 40% longer summarization flows
- Latency SLO: p95 generation < 450ms (interactive)

Specific asks:
1) Units-per-dollar range (tokens/$) for a realistic configuration (batching + prefix cache)
2) Where caching helps vs where batching is the dominant lever for Helio’s traffic
3) Any blockers in the eval plan that would blow cost assumptions (e.g., KV cache warmup times, cold-start behavior)

Attached: Helio_Pilot_Traffic.xlsx (traffic profile + sample prompts).

We need a short MAP entry with final numbers and gating criteria (cost tolerances + perf tradeoffs) by end of day Friday so procurement can begin PO prep.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Integrations
HelioHealth

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. I pulled a quick first-pass sanity check and sketched a MAP draft (attached). High-level notes below; will iterate once Ben/Karthik add ops/infra inputs.

Short answer (first-pass): with prefix caching + conservative batching we should target a working units/$ band of ~9k–13k tokens per $ for the workload described (varies with hit rate + average response length). That maps to an estimated monthly spend of $3.5k–$9k for the pilot footprint you shared (assuming 2 million tokens/month baseline; exact #s in attached).

Key assumptions I used in the draft:
- Baseline model: open-variant, 8-bit quantized, supports streaming
- avg tokens per request: 300 (in+out)
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV): 45% for short Q&A; 10% for summarization flows
- Effective batching window: 15–25ms under normal traffic; falls to 40–60ms at 250–400 req/s
- Latency tradeoff: to maintain p95 < 450ms we recommend a max batching latency budget of 25ms and prefetching warmed KV entries for known templates

MAP draft attached as MAP-draft.pdf — includes a mutual action list: simulation, MAP signoff, pilot SOW + payment terms.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to confirm operational batch sizing and the expected tokens/$ numbers once sim results are in
- Karthik to validate cache warmup and edge-case cold-start impact for your peak bursts
- We sync Monday for a MAP walk-through and final numbers so procurement can start PO language

I'll also attach a tiny sim file with the rough math; Ben will add more detailed sim notes.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Looping in a few quick ops/ops-questions from my side — high level only so we don't overpromise: 

- Batching: for the traffic profile, our recommended production config is adaptive batching with an upper batch-size cap that keeps p95 < 450ms. In practice that means target batch windows of 20ms and a hard cap of 100 tokens-per-batch. If Helio values latency > cost, we can reduce target window to 10–15ms but tokens/$ drops ~10–15%.

- Caching: prefix cache helps massively on short Q&A. If you can parameterize prompts into templates and attach stable prefixes, hit rates >50% are realistic. But for summarization the cache helps less (10–20%). Hit rate delta moves tokens/$ by ~25–40% depending on workload mix.

- Cold starts: GPU pool cold starts are rare on Dedicated, but for Hosted we need an autoscale buffer (we suggest 10% reserved burst capacity). Cold KV warmup (first 2–5 minutes of a new traffic pattern) can spike costs — this should be reflected as a MAP risk item.

Attached quick notes from a small batching sim I ran: batching-sim-notes.txt

Questions for Helio:
1) Can you share examples of templated prompts vs free-form inputs? (this helps estimate cacheable fraction)
2) Do you have any hard SLA beyond the latency p95 (e.g., streaming start times)?

Ben

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick sanity check: units/$ assumptions for pilot

Quick technical input from infra/eval perspective — adding a few gating items I want captured in the MAP so we don't get surprised mid-pilot: 

- Cache warmup profile: record expected warmup window (minutes) and include a safety multiplier for first-week runs. I'll propose we model a 3x token consumption during warmup in the MAP until we have observed hit-rates.

- Sequence length distribution: the attached spreadsheet needs a per-journey token histogram (not just average). That materially changes batching efficiency and GPU kernel selection. If Helio can provide percentiles we'll run a micro-sim and publish tokens/$ per percentile bucket.

- Prefetch strategy: for known templates we can precompute and load KV entries before traffic spikes (works well for scheduled workflows). For ad-hoc summarization it's trickier. Add prefetch as a MAP action: 'precompute top 20 templates for initial pilot cohorts'.

- Metric hooks for eval: include tracked metrics in MAP: tokens consumed, cache hit rate, avg batching window, p95 latency, and per-route cost. We'll provide a lightweight dashboard.

I dropped a short sim folder with a starter workload into the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bHelioPilotSim (internal only). I can run a 24h sim if you want — gives a more concrete tokens/$ distribution.

Karthik
Principal SW Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks, team — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of quick decisions from Helio:

- We'll prioritize template-driven Q&A for pilot cohort A (customer success flows) — we expect cacheable fraction to be ~55% there. Summarization cohort B will be separate and instrumented only for the eval period.
- Procurement is comfortable with a MAP that includes a 3x warmup multiplier for the first 72 hours and a contingency holdback if monthly tokens deviate +30% vs forecast.

Requests: can Redwood produce a one-page MAP summary with final tokens/$ bands, the gating list (cache warmup, prefetch actions, batch window caps), and the eval plan (what you'll instrument and when)? We need that one-pager to attach to the SOW and internal procurement memo. Also please include the HubSpot deal id HL-337 so my finance team can cross-reference.

We can do a 30-min call Monday to walk the MAP and sign off. Can you send a calendar invite?
